title: The TOP-SCOPE Survey of Planck Galactic Cold Clumps: Molecular gas properties
summary: We surveyed 2008 Planck Galactic Cold Clumps (PGCCs) in $^{12}\mathrm{CO}$ and $^{13}\mathrm{CO}$ $J=1$--0 lines using the Taeduk Radio Astronomy Observatory (TRAO) 14 m telescope's multi-beam receiver. We detected 2784 ($^{12}\mathrm{CO}$) and 2291 ($^{13}\mathrm{CO}$) velocity components, their closely correlated centroid velocities suggest that $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO generally trace kinematically associated gas. PGCCs have low excitation temperatures (mean $\sim$10 K), mean $^{13}\mathrm{CO}$ optical depth $\sim$0.5, and mean $^{13}\mathrm{CO}$-derived H$_2$ column density $4.3\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$. Gas--dust correlations are moderate, with $N_{^{13}\mathrm{CO}}$ more tightly correlated with the dust-derived H$_2$ column density from the PGCC catalog than $I_{^{12}\mathrm{CO}}$. Colder PGCCs tend to have higher CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor ($X_{\mathrm{CO}}$) and $[\mathrm{H_{2}}]/[^{13}\mathrm{CO}]$ ratio. $X_{\mathrm{CO}}$ increases clearly with the dust-derived H$_2$ column density, consistent with enhanced CO freeze-out in high-column-density gas. Supersonic non-thermal motions are widespread: the Mach number derived from $^{13}\mathrm{CO}$ has a mean of 4.3 and a median of 3.6, increasing slightly with dust-derived H$_2$ column density. Overall, PGCCs are cold but dynamically active, serving as a valuable laboratory for studying the initial conditions of star formation.

AI.tldr: This study surveys 2008 Planck Galactic Cold Clumps (PGCCs) in CO lines using the TRAO 14 m telescope, detecting thousands of velocity components. PGCCs exhibit low excitation temperatures (~10 K), moderate optical depths, and supersonic non-thermal motions (mean Mach number 4.3). The CO-to-H2 conversion factor increases with column density, consistent with CO freeze-out, and the clumps serve as cold but dynamically active laboratories for studying star formation initial conditions.
AI.motivation: To characterize the physical properties of Planck Galactic Cold Clumps (PGCCs) in molecular gas tracers, including excitation temperature, column density, CO-to-H2 conversion factor, and gas-dust correlations, in order to understand the initial conditions of star formation.
AI.method: A survey of 2008 PGCCs was conducted in 12CO and 13CO J=1-0 lines using the TRAO 14 m telescope with a multi-beam receiver. Velocity components were identified, and physical parameters (excitation temperature, optical depth, H2 column density, CO-to-H2 conversion factor, Mach numbers) were derived and correlated with dust-derived properties.
AI.result: 2784 (12CO) and 2291 (13CO) velocity components were detected with closely correlated centroid velocities. PGCCs have mean excitation temperature ~10 K, mean 13CO optical depth ~0.5, and mean H2 column density 4.3x10^21 cm^-2. Gas-dust correlations were moderate; colder clumps have higher X_CO and H2/13CO ratios. X_CO increases with column density, and supersonic non-thermal motions are widespread with mean Mach number 4.3.
AI.conclusion: PGCCs are cold but dynamically active clumps. The increasing X_CO with column density supports enhanced CO freeze-out in dense gas. Their combination of low temperatures and supersonic turbulence makes them valuable laboratories for investigating the initial conditions of star formation.
